rationale: F084 is the guardrail in front of the attachment switch that F002 now contains: it only inspects PDFs that arrive through that switch, has nothing to act on without it, and by Tony's own rule (recorded on F023 and in F084's caveats) the gate has to be proven before the switch is turned on, so the two are one decision. Both are wave A on the parents' own agents, the card states the gate's limit (PDFs with readable text only; scans and photos pass unchecked) and keeps F002's medium risk, and round 1 left this pairing as a merge hint on both records without deciding it.
name: Photos and PDFs sent to Happy are read and answered, behind a local privacy gate for text PDFs (attachment intake switched on)

rationale: Both are the roadmap's single 'Voice (iMessage)' capability, speech-to-text in and text-to-speech out on the Mac mini with no cloud speech service, and the spoken reply's main trigger is the voice memo that F003 brings in. VOX-04's record gives no dependency or risk reason for wave C (its first step uses the built-in macOS voice with no install and its only catalog dependency is F003), neither half adds a way to send data out, and the card keeps F003's medium risk and names the neural voice and its engine choice as a later step.
name: Voice over iMessage, all on the Mac mini: voice memos transcribed locally, spoken replies in a local voice (macOS say first, a neural voice later, cloud speech off)

rationale: Both turn a date in a message or a photographed flyer into a reminder or a calendar entry only after the parent says yes, and F011's own record says its calendar half waits on F010. Both are wave B on the parent's own agent, and the card states the read-and-propose part and the calendar write (a tap-to-add calendar file first, a direct write with approval later) separately and carries F010's high risk, so the write is not hidden.
name: Dates into reminders and the family calendar after a yes: from a typed request, a flyer photo or a PDF (tap-to-add calendar file first, direct calendar write later)

rationale: Both give the family National Weather Service weather for home, one as an answer on request and one as a heads-up on a new alert, and F083's own record says it earns its place as the weather feed for the watch and would be built together with it. Both are low risk, hold no private data and add no recipient, and nothing in wave A depends on F083, so the pair ships in wave B without overriding any dependency or risk reason.
name: Home weather from the National Weather Service: hourly rain and snow on request, and a heads-up on each new severe-weather alert with the school-night and chore lines

rationale: Both hand the memory-less research agent a short brief (a budget, ages, dates) and return a few options with links, the price, hours or dates where the page could be read and the time it was fetched, leaving the buying and booking to the parent. Both are wave C and low risk on the same agent with only ages, date ranges and a distance crossing over, and the Places lookup (F021) stays its own card because it needs a Google key with billing switched on, which is a separate decision.
name: Options research with sources: products, camps and classes, outings and trips (parents buy and book)

rationale: Both end in the same place, a dinner's ingredients offered to the shared grocery list after a yes, and a recipe taken from a link is the natural entry for the recipe box that F033's Sunday plan draws on. Neither wave rests on a dependency or a new kind of risk (everything each needs is in wave A), the untrusted recipe page stays with the research agent while the plan and the list stay on the parent's agent, and the card says so and carries F033's medium risk.
name: Meals to grocery list: recipe links reduced to ingredients and steps, a recipe box, and a Sunday dinner plan

rationale: Since round 1 moved the tax checklist onto the owner's read-only mail agent, both are the same job pattern: an isolated scheduled run on that agent with the read-only Gmail tool that texts only the mailbox owner, and both wait on the same open decision about personal mail on the cloud model. Same wave, agent, account grant and medium risk, read-only in both halves, so nothing riskier is hidden; the school mailbox and the on-demand mail lookup stay separate cards.
name: Scheduled read-only inbox reports for each adult: the 07:00 action-items digest, and a January-to-April Saturday tax-form arrival check

rationale: Both are the parents' weekly look at Happy's own activity, what it did and what it saved to memory, sent to the same adults on the same Sunday in the same wave, and a memory save is itself a tool action of the kind the digest reports. Neither gives any agent a new tool, recipient or data source, forgetting a conversation stays an operator command at the Mac, and the card carries F085's medium risk.
name: What Happy did and what it remembered: a review on request and each Sunday, with forgetting a conversation on request

rationale: Both keep track of the documents other people demand for the children (the immunization record and physical for school and camp, passport validity and a consent letter for travel), warn before the date that matters, and draft text for a parent to sign and submit. Both are wave C and medium risk on the parent's own agent over the household store, nothing leaves the family, and in neither does Happy fill in, sign, certify or book anything.
name: Children's paperwork kit: enrolment, camp and health forms, and travel documents before a trip

rationale: Talk mode is a feature of the same App Store app on the same phone, reached through the same pairing, command deny list and access-level decision that OCL-01 describes, and VOX-01's own record defers to OCL-01 for all of it. Both are wave D, high risk and limited to Tony's phone, so nothing riskier is hidden, and realtime voice (VOX-02) stays its own card because round 1 found it a separate decision (raw audio to OpenAI on its own key).
name: OpenClaw iPhone app on Tony's phone: pairing with device commands denied first, chat with files, tap approvals and Talk mode (operator only)
